props.title: Top 67 Claude Skills That Turn a $20 Subscription Into a Full Dev Team
props.thesis: The full-team headline is marketing. The real mechanism is a folder of instructions and examples that keeps a workflow alive between sessions.
props.take: Adopt in stages, and judge a skill on the tasks you actually fail.

narration: Sixty-seven skills, and a headline that promises a whole development team. [pause] Set the promise aside. The mechanism underneath is genuinely useful. A skill is a folder. It holds instructions, examples, constraints, and sometimes scripts. That is what makes a workflow survive between sessions. [pause] The author suggests a staged order. Start by making skills. Skill Creator turns your bullet points into a draft. You then run a handful of test prompts, and fix whatever fails. [pause] Next, planning. Grill Me interrogates your requirements, including data models and failure cases. Write a P R D combines an interview with codebase exploration. P R D to Plan sequences thin vertical slices. P R D to Issues turns them into assignable work. [pause] Then engineering discipline. Test-driven development. Systematic debugging — reproduce, isolate, one fix, verify. [pause] Then repository safety, which is the part people skip. Git Guardrails adds hooks that block push, hard reset and clean before they run. Pre-commit assembles linting, type checks and tests. [pause] Beyond code, the list reaches further. A documentation generator derives OpenAPI material straight from your routes. Theme Factory turns a brand description into palette tokens. An Excel server drives spreadsheets without desktop Excel. [pause] Judge any of these on the tasks you actually fail. Not on the headline.
